compiled_state.title: Multiple CI workflows gated to base=main don't fire on sub-branch PRs (same pattern as llm-review gap)
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

Several CI workflows have `pull_request: branches: [main]` triggers, meaning they only fire on PRs that target main. PRs targeting session branches (sprint sub-PRs and debug-everything batch PRs) do not trigger these workflows. Failures only surface at the session→main PR stage — sometimes blocking the merge cascade with bugs that the per-sub-PR CI would have caught.

## Evidence (this session, 2026-05-18)

- PR #227 (story 5621 → session) and PR #228 (story 7034 → session) both PASSED Script Tests CI
- PR #231 (session → main) FAILED "Python Skill/Doc Tests" CI on first run
- The failure was triggered by multi-test RED zone markers (`[test_a,test_b,test_c]`) in `.test-index` causing the pytest -k builder in `tests/skills/run-python-tests.sh` to produce invalid syntax. The .test-index entries were added in story 5621 (sub-PR #227) but the Python Skill/Doc Tests job did not fire on PR #227 because its base was the session branch, not main.

## Affected workflows (audit 2026-05-18)

- `.github/workflows/ci-python-skills.yml` — `pull_request: branches: [main]` (lines 26-28)
- `.github/workflows/portability-smoke.yml` — gated similarly
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the `llm-review` job uses `if: github.base_ref == 'main'` (lines 312-314); the WHOLE workflow runs on sub-branch PRs but the llm-review job within it does not. (Same pattern, different mechanism.)

Other workflows to audit during remediation:
- `.github/workflows/inbound-bridge.yml`
- `.github/workflows/outbound-bridge.yml`
- `.github/workflows/template-real-url-e2e.yml`
- `.github/workflows/ticket-platform-matrix.yml`
- `.github/workflows/ticket-perf-regression.yml`
- `.github/workflows/ticket-lifecycle.yml`

## Why this is P1

- The user has repeatedly stated that smaller-diff sub-PR review is load-bearing for reliable LLM review of large epics. The same principle applies to ANY CI check: catching a bug at the per-sub-PR boundary is cheaper than catching it at the session→main merge boundary.
- Bugs caught at session→main block the merge cascade and force back-and-forth with multiple branches (this session: had to merge session back into 7034 after the runner.py and local_workflow.py fixes, resolving conflicts).
- This is the SAME root architectural pattern as the missing per-sub-PR llm-review (post-mortem bug 576b-a6c7-3de3-4eef).

## Suggested remediation

Roll into the remediation epic. The fix is to extend the `pull_request` triggers in main-gated workflows to ALSO fire on sub-branch targets. Specifically:
- `pull_request: branches: [main, 'session/**', 'story/**']` (or wildcard `branches: ['*']` if appropriate)
- For `ci.yml`'s `llm-review` job: drop the `base_ref == 'main'` filter OR add a parallel branch in the `if:` for sub-branch targets

This is the SAME architectural change as the per-sub-PR llm-review gap fix — they should be addressed together in the remediation epic.

## Related
- Companion architectural bug: 576b-a6c7-3de3-4eef (per-sub-PR llm-review gap)
- Surfaced during: epic b575 merge cascade (session→main PR #231 Python Skill/Doc Tests failure)
- Tracked under no parent epic (will be rolled into remediation epic SCs)
